mission: The empty chamber becomes a live mystery: someone escaped from inside and has already had time to move.
why_now: The archive revelation of R04a has set the terms; now the physical evidence of an already-loose anchor gives the revelation its forward pressure. The mystery of the escapee is what pulls Ben off-ridge toward the Corridor.
conflict: The chamber shows systematic, patient escape — centuries of work, methodical, intelligent. Ben needs a name and the archive will not give him one. Sera examines the erosion pattern and is visibly thrown by what she sees. Torin, who should be reading the residue most clearly, says something mildly wrong — a single beat of inflection Ben cannot quite place, which seeds H06 per D7 without telegraphing.
turning_point: Ben understands that whoever escaped has had time to move and has been moving. The question of who is deferred; the question of how far is immediate. The escapee is already out there. H06 plants through Torin — a warmth-adjacent line that sits one degree off from where it should.
opening_hook: The monitoring logs for the empty chamber span centuries — a slow, patient record of something working its way out from inside. The readable portions end abruptly twenty-three standard days back. The rest is corrupted in a way Desh does not like
closing_hook: An escapee without a name. Twenty-three standard days of silence on the logs. Torin's one inflection that Ben cannot quite place. Ben tells Desh to pull every monitoring packet and start reconstructing — answer first light
emotional_trajectory: Investigative tension -> dawning unease at the scope of what has already happened -> forward pressure

stakes.personal: Ben is now responsible for stopping someone who has already been moving for weeks without the galaxy knowing
stakes.interpersonal: Torin's faintly-off inflection registers for Ben as a warmth detail that does not quite sit; he does not interpret it, he files it
stakes.external: The seal is failing and an anchor is already loose in the Corridor

setting: Fortress Level 3 — the empty chamber, then monitoring station on Level 1
sensory_details: Damage inside the empty chamber not frantic but systematic — deliberate erosion carried on for centuries; Gavran's monitoring flags lit red and unanswered; the residue the escapee left in the Force different in quality from the three survivors — still, analytical, patient in a way that makes Ben's shoulders tighten; Sera's precision breaking because the workmanship feels familiar before the name is allowed into the story; Kael's gaze catching on the same patience and going flatter, recognizing a fellow captive's discipline without forgiving what it became; Torin's breath at the doorway, a half-smile at something Ben cannot see
canon_elements_needed: Brotherhood of Darkness era stasis infrastructure
Archive language/register guardrail: use archaic Basic, High Galactic legal script, or pre-Reformation administrative Basic; avoid non-canon ancient-language labels
Stasis chamber escape mechanics and Force erosion techniques
action_beats: Ben pulls up the empty chamber's monitoring logs on the flickering display — readable until twenty-three standard days ago, corrupted after
Desh catalogues signs of the escapee's post-escape activity — accessed terminals, moved equipment, supplies taken — without being able to put a name on the pattern
Sera examines the erosion marks and her precision-register breaks for a half-second; she steadies, does not explain, because naming the craft would name a person the chapter is withholding
Kael studies the same marks from farther back and says nothing, but the silence changes texture: not ignorance, recognition withheld

Torin stands at the doorway and makes a small warmth-adjacent observation that is one inflection off — H06 plants. It catches in Ben like a wrong note in familiar music, and he does not yet have a place to put it
Ben overlays the escapee's activity timestamps on the fortress map — the pattern is methodical, the name is withheld, the Corridor is the direction
notes: Keep the absence sharper than the explanation. Sera and Kael may show recognition of a kind of mind or craft, but not the escapee's name. Torin's off note should register and pass, not ring like a warning bell.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Ben understands that whoever escaped has had time to move and has been moving — the readable monitoring logs end twenty-three standard days ago, and the physical evidence of systematic activity (accessed terminals, moved equipment, supplies taken) proves the escapee did not simply vanish.
turning_point_detail.shift: The question of identity is deferred; the question of how far is immediate. The escapee is already out there, already moving. The scene pivots from investigation to forward pressure. H06 plants through Torin's warmth-adjacent line that sits one degree off from where it should.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben is now responsible for stopping someone who has already been moving for weeks without the galaxy knowing. Torin's faintly-off inflection registers as a warmth detail that does not quite sit; Ben files it without interpretation, seeding doubt he cannot yet name.

emotional_arc.start: Investigative tension — focused, methodical, pushing toward action rather than explanation.
emotional_arc.shift: Dawning unease at the scope of what has already happened — the realization that weeks have passed, that the escapee has had time to move, that the threat is not theoretical but already in motion.
emotional_arc.end: Forward pressure — braced, locked into the next phase, responsibility settling onto Ben's shoulders.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben pulls up the empty chamber's monitoring logs on the flickering display — readable until twenty-three standard days ago, then corrupted.
key_beats.state_change: Abstract threat becomes concrete: the logs provide a timeline. The readable portion ends abruptly; the corruption pattern suggests deliberate erasure or system failure, not accident.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's investigative tension sharpens into focus — the instinct to act, to move forward, to find the next piece. His shoulders register the weight of what the logs are not saying.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh catalogs the physical evidence of post-escape activity: accessed terminals, moved equipment, supplies taken. The pattern is methodical, but Desh cannot put a name to it.
key_beats.state_change: The escapee's presence becomes undeniable and recent. The activity is not frantic; it is patient, intelligent, systematic. Someone has been moving through the fortress with purpose.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's unease deepens — the scope of what has already happened crystallizes. His focus tightens on the timeline: weeks of activity, weeks of preparation, weeks of advantage. His breath steadies; his mind accelerates.

key_beats.beat_description: Sera examines the erosion marks inside the chamber — the damage pattern that shows centuries of work, methodical and patient. Her precision-register breaks for a half-second; she steadies herself and does not explain what she saw.
key_beats.state_change: The technical evidence confirms the emotional pressure: whoever escaped did not break out in desperation. They worked their way free with patience that spans centuries. Sera's reaction — the momentary loss of composure — signals that the implications are larger than the immediate escape.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Sera's break in composure catches Ben without his needing to ask. The unease settles deeper: if Sera is shaken, the threat is not routine. His shoulders tighten; he does not press her. The silence between them carries weight.

key_beats.beat_description: Torin stands at the doorway, observing the chamber. He makes a small observation — something warmth-adjacent, a detail that sits one inflection off from where it should. It catches in Ben like a wrong note in familiar music, and he files it without interpretation.
key_beats.state_change: H06 plants. The scene pivots: the question of identity defers; the question of how far becomes immediate. The escapee is already out there. Torin's off-note does not ring as a warning; it passes, but it does not settle.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's attention catches on Torin's inflection — not alarm, but a small dissonance that his mind cannot quite place. He does not interpret it; he files it. The unease has a new shape now, one he cannot yet name. His focus remains on the forward pressure, but Torin's warmth-adjacent line sits in the corner of his awareness, waiting.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben overlays the escapee's activity timestamps on the fortress map. The pattern is methodical, the direction clear: the Corridor. The name remains withheld.
key_beats.state_change: The next phase locks in. The escapee is not a mystery to be solved in the chamber; they are a moving target already weeks ahead. The fortress is no longer the primary theater. The Corridor is.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Forward pressure settles onto Ben as responsibility. He is braced for the handoff, for the next phase. His voice is steady when he tells Desh to pull every monitoring packet and start reconstructing — answer first light. The weight of what he now knows, and what he still does not, settles across his shoulders.

anti_patterns: Keep the absence sharper than the explanation — do not name what the evidence means; let it accumulate.
Do not ring Torin's off note like a warning bell — it should register and pass without interpretation.
Avoid diagnostic voice when describing the Force-residue the escapee left behind; keep it sensory and experiential.
Use archaic Basic, High Galactic legal script, or pre-Reformation administrative Basic for monitoring logs or chamber text.
Do not arrive at clinical articulation of what the scope of the escape means; let Ben's shoulders and breath register it first.
